sections.heading: Results
sections.lead: Reducing regulatory and administrative constraints, and enhancing market entry and expansion — the two strands of one intervention that turns formal recognition into genuine economic participation.

body: This area targets the registration-to-compliance journey directly, delivered in collaboration with the government partners who hold each mandate.

sections.heading: Regulatory & administrative constraints
prose: Through our MOU with the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection, CECF identifies unregistered self-help groups, CBOs, welfare associations and faith-based networks, and supports their registration under the Community Groups Registration Act 2022 — directly closing the awareness gap keeping most grassroots groups outside legal protection.
Partnering with the Business Registration Service, group businesses and MSMEs move from informal to legally recognised entities able to open accounts, sign contracts and bid for tenders.
With the Kenya Revenue Authority, groups receive tax registration support and simplified education on new eTIMS invoicing and Finance Act 2025 reporting requirements.
secondColumnProse: Through the National Judiciary’s Mediation Department, groups gain continuous training in resolving business-related conflicts internally — addressing a key driver of group collapse once shared financial resources are introduced.

media.alt: Two parties in mediation across a table

sections.heading: Digital consolidation of services
sections.body: CECF’s digital platform unifies the above, allowing individuals, groups and MSMEs to self-register, track applications and link directly to negotiated government services — collapsing a fragmented, multi-counter process into a single digital journey.
**Government fees are paid to the issuing body at its published rate.** CECF does not add to them, and our assistance is free.

sections.heading: Market entry & expansion
prose: ### Financial literacy paired with negotiated products

With Kingdom Bank and I&M Bank, staged financial literacy training — savings, budgeting, digital safety, bookkeeping — unlocks matched, negotiated financial products such as low-minimum savings accounts and alternative-underwriting group loans.

Through Britam Insurance, groups access affordable, group-based micro-insurance tailored to informal-sector income patterns, protecting formalisation and market gains against shocks such as illness, death or business loss.

sections.heading: Simplified, replicable licensing
body: Building on CECF’s Nairobi County licensing partnership, the model is documented and replicated into additional counties, prioritising those with the highest exclusion rates.

sections.heading: Aggregation and market-linkage infrastructure
body: Our digital platform aggregates dispersed, formalised groups into a pool that larger buyers, financial institutions and procurement systems can engage directly, while a small grants fund channels capital toward groups demonstrating genuine growth potential.

sections.heading: Financial literacy comes first
sections.body: Credit offered to a group that cannot read its own books is not opportunity — it is a debt trap with a ceremony attached. Every group referred to a financial partner has been through practical training first: what a loan actually costs, how to read a statement, what happens if a member defaults, and how to decide as a group whether to borrow at all. **Some groups finish that training and decide not to borrow. We count that as a success.**

sections.heading: Bring your group or MSME in
sections.body: Assistance is free. Bring what you have — we will tell you plainly what is missing and what it will cost, before you spend anything.
